whoIsThisFor.heading: Who may use these Education Cloud Consultant study notes?

personas.label: Higher education CRM consultants
personas.description: You help colleges and universities turn student, admissions, advancement, and constituent needs into Salesforce designs.

personas.label: Salesforce administrators at educational institutions
personas.description: You support education-focused Salesforce solutions and want organized notes on implementation and product choices.

personas.label: Education technology partners
personas.description: You work with education customers on requirements, integrations, data governance, and adoption.

examDifficulty.heading: How should you use the Education Cloud Consultant exam guide?
examDifficulty.summary: Salesforce’s published guide describes the Salesforce Certified Education Cloud Consultant exam. Registration and delivery have ended, and Salesforce lists retirement effective February 1, 2027. Treat these details as a historical reference rather than an active exam syllabus.
bullets: Published format: 60 multiple-choice questions plus up to five unscored questions in 105 minutes; the published passing score is 67%.
Published fees: US$200 registration and US$100 retake; JPY 30,000 for each, plus applicable local tax.
Availability: Registration ended July 24, 2026, and the last exam date was August 31, 2026.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: This exam is no longer available for registration or delivery. For current Education and Agentforce Education learning, use Salesforce documentation and Trailhead materials rather than treating this historical exam outline as a current syllabus.

examFormat.heading: Historical Education Cloud Consultant exam format
examFormat.intro: The published exam guide lists the format below; registration and exam delivery have ended.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Salesforce does not publish a scenario-question percentage. The historical domains cover requirements-based solution design, configuration, implementation strategy, integration and data management, and analytics.
bestWayToPass: Start with institutional needs: Identify users, processes, constraints, data ownership, intended outcomes, and existing systems.
Confirm the product and data model: Distinguish the Education Cloud platform solution from Education Data Architecture package deployments and verify details in current documentation.
Plan implementation and adoption: Consider governance, change management, staffing, testing, deployment, and long-term support.
Design integrations around ownership: Document the source of truth for each data element, exchange timing, error handling, privacy, and migration needs.

certificationCard.description: Historical reference for Salesforce’s education implementation consultant credential. Salesforce now calls the product Agentforce Education; the published exam guide reflects a Winter ’24 domain outline and is not a current exam syllabus.

keyConcepts.h2: Education Consultant: product and data-model study notes

blocks.heading: Education Data Architecture and Product Choice
blocks.body: Education Data Architecture (EDA) is a managed-package data model for education. Salesforce distinguishes it from the Education Cloud platform solution, now called Agentforce Education. Before applying assumptions about records or relationships, establish which product and model the institution uses. Check that product’s current documentation for object names, behavior, and supported features.

blocks.heading: Student Success Workflows
blocks.body: Design student success capabilities around institutional goals, staff responsibilities, access policies, available data, and intervention processes. Confirm which licensed features the institution has and how they work before specifying alerts, cases, appointments, or plans. The technology should support a defined student support process and its follow-up.

blocks.heading: Recruitment and Admissions
blocks.body: Recruitment and admissions processes can span initial interest, application, review, decision, and enrollment. Map the actual institutional workflow, records, portal needs, staff handoffs, and interfaces to application systems. Requirements and product configuration vary, so verify how the chosen Education solution supports each step.

blocks.heading: Experience Cloud for Students and Faculty
blocks.body: An online portal can give learners or faculty access to selected information and interactions. Portal scope depends on product, licenses, configuration, and security requirements. Define which audiences can see which records, then validate the proposed experience and sharing model in current documentation.

blocks.heading: Integrating Student and Learning Systems
blocks.body: For student information systems (SIS), learning management systems (LMS), and other sources, define which system owns each data element, which direction data moves, and how often it is exchanged. Plan reconciliation, error handling, privacy, access, and migration quality. Different institutions may use different systems of record, so avoid assuming one pattern fits all.

scenarioTips.intro: These prompts summarize themes from the published guide and are not predictions about any current exam. Confirm product behavior and terminology in current documentation.

blocks.heading: Identify the Data Model
blocks.body: Determine whether the scenario uses the EDA managed package or the Education Cloud platform solution. Then verify account models and relationships for that product.

blocks.heading: Map the Student Journey
blocks.body: Trace the institution’s processes from recruitment and admissions through student success and alumni engagement. Identify the users and handoffs at each stage.

blocks.heading: Model Programs and Courses
blocks.body: Use requirements to identify program, course, and enrollment information. Verify object names and relationships against the data model selected for the institution.

blocks.heading: Design Advising Workflows
blocks.body: Clarify the goal, relevant signals, assigned staff, access rules, follow-up process, and licensed features before configuring an advising solution.

blocks.heading: Connect Reporting to Decisions
blocks.body: Identify who will use each report and what decision it supports. Check data quality, access, governance, and volume before selecting an analytics approach.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Related credentials for education solution consultants
nextCertsAfter.intro: For current learning, consider platform administration or a role-focused Salesforce credential that matches your implementation work.

sampleQuestions.question: In the described education data model, where is a prospective student with no organization affiliation represented?
options: As an org user with a portal license
As a contact under a placeholder account
As a lead until the student accepts an offer
As a person account
sampleQuestions.explanation: The study example represents an unaffiliated person as a person account. Confirm the model used by the institution before applying this pattern.
whyWrong: An applicant does not need an internal Salesforce user record merely to be represented as a person.
A placeholder account is not the model choice described in this example.
A lead may suit some processes, but it is not the answer in this specific study scenario.

sampleQuestions.question: What does an affiliation record capture in an education data model?
options: A connection between a person and an organization
The courses a student takes during one academic term
The advisor assigned to support a student
The financial aid package awarded to a student
sampleQuestions.explanation: An affiliation represents a relationship between a person and an organization, such as an institution or employer.
whyWrong: This describes the relationship captured by an affiliation.
Course participation is represented through academic program and course records.
An advisor relationship is a separate assignment.

sampleQuestions.question: A learner joins a degree program and takes six courses within it. Which structure best represents this?
options: An opportunity for the program with six product lines
One affiliation listing all courses in its description
A program enrollment connected to the course records
Six separate program enrollments, one for each course
sampleQuestions.explanation: A program enrollment represents participation in the program and can relate to the courses taken, subject to the selected data model.
whyWrong: Opportunities represent sales processes and do not model academic participation in this example.
An affiliation links a person to an organization rather than listing course enrollment.
One enrollment per course would confuse course participation with program enrollment.

sampleQuestions.question: Why might an education solution represent a household as well as an individual student?
options: Family members may participate in decisions and giving
Course connections require every student to belong to a household
Regulations require each home address to use a separate object
A person account cannot store more than one address
sampleQuestions.explanation: Households can help represent family relationships that matter to education decisions and advancement activity.
whyWrong: Course relationships do not universally require a household record.
This is not a general regulatory requirement for modeling addresses.
Address handling depends on the chosen data model and does not by itself require a household.

sampleQuestions.question: An admissions team needs to track an application through review, interview, and decision. Which record best fits the process in this example?
options: A task for each stage
A case for each application step
A program enrollment for each stage
An application record with stages
sampleQuestions.explanation: An application record can track the applicant’s progress through the defined admissions stages.
whyWrong: Tasks may support assigned work but do not replace the application lifecycle record.
Cases manage service issues and are not the application process record described here.
Program enrollment applies after admission when the student participates in a program.

sampleQuestions.question: What does an advisor relationship record describe?
options: The advisor’s employment contract
Which advisor supports a student and how
Fees charged for advising
The courses the advisor teaches
sampleQuestions.explanation: The relationship identifies which advisor supports the student and the capacity of that support.
whyWrong: An advisor’s employment contract belongs in personnel records.
Fees are not the purpose of a student-advisor relationship record.
Teaching assignments are separate from identifying a student’s advisor.

sampleQuestions.question: A student pauses study and returns the following year. How should the institution preserve the history?
options: Delete the original enrollment and recreate it on return
Keep the history and record the new enrollment period
Create a second person account for the returning student
Remove the gap from the affiliation record
sampleQuestions.explanation: Retaining the original history and recording the new period preserves the student’s timeline.
whyWrong: Deleting the original enrollment would erase useful academic history.
The returning learner is the same person, so a second person account would fragment their history.
Editing out the gap would hide a meaningful period in the student’s record.

sampleQuestions.question: Why model the structure of colleges, faculties, and departments?
options: It can reflect how the institution’s units relate to each other
It determines which employees can log in
It sets the order in which applicants receive offers
It calculates tuition for every program
sampleQuestions.explanation: An organizational hierarchy can represent how institutional units are arranged and related.
whyWrong: Login access is controlled through user and permission settings.
Admissions offers are handled by the admissions process, not organizational nesting.
Tuition is determined by program and pricing rules, not by hierarchy alone.

sampleQuestions.question: An institution wants to learn which recruitment events are associated with later enrollments. What data link helps answer this?
options: Ask each enrolled student to remember every event
Compare yearly event counts with total enrollment
Connect event attendance with the application record
Count attendance at each event
sampleQuestions.explanation: Linking attendance to the application allows the institution to analyze event participation alongside application outcomes.
whyWrong: Asking people to remember events may produce incomplete information.
Comparing aggregate event and enrollment totals cannot link an attendee to an outcome.
Attendance counts show event reach but not the later enrollment of each attendee.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the difference between a course and a course offering?
options: The course is undergraduate; the offering is postgraduate
The course is in-person; the offering is online
The course defines the subject; the offering is a specific run of it
Faculty create the course; admissions creates the offering
sampleQuestions.explanation: A course defines the academic subject, while an offering represents a particular instance or run of that course.
whyWrong: The distinction does not depend on undergraduate or postgraduate level.
A course and its offering can have different delivery modes.
The difference is not based on which team creates each record.

sampleQuestions.question: A client built a custom object to store student data. What should the consultant assess first?
options: Whether enough custom object capacity remains
Whether the custom object can be renamed to the standard name
Whether the data should be moved to another org
Whether the standard model already meets the requirement
sampleQuestions.explanation: Compare the requirement with the available standard data model before deciding whether custom storage is needed.
whyWrong: Capacity does not establish whether the data model fits the requirement.
Renaming a custom object does not give it standard object behavior.
A separate org is not the first step in assessing a data model.

sampleQuestions.question: Why use program enrollment records rather than opportunities to track a learner’s participation?
options: Opportunities cannot store start and end dates
Enrollment represents ongoing study, not a sales deal
Only program enrollment can link to a person account
Education records cannot be reported with opportunities
sampleQuestions.explanation: Program enrollment represents a learner’s participation in an academic program rather than a prospective sales transaction.
whyWrong: Opportunities can store dates; that is not the reason to use enrollment.
The relationship to a person depends on the chosen data model.
Education data can be reported; reporting is not the key distinction.

sampleQuestions.question: An alumni team wants to view giving activity alongside a person’s academic history. What supports this?
options: A separate alumni database synced nightly
A second person account created after graduation
The same person record can relate to both histories
A rule that locks academic records at graduation
sampleQuestions.explanation: Keeping one person identity connected to academic and advancement information supports a broader relationship view, subject to access controls.
whyWrong: A separate database can fragment history and requires synchronization.
A second person account could split one individual’s records.
Locking records does not connect academic and giving data.

sampleQuestions.question: What should a consultant establish before designing an education data model?
options: Which analytics product will be used after go-live
Map the institution and student journey
How many custom fields the legacy system contains
Which license each staff member currently has
sampleQuestions.explanation: Understanding the institution and its student lifecycle provides the context for selecting a suitable model.
whyWrong: Reporting tools matter, but first understand the institution’s structure and process.
Legacy field counts do not explain the institution’s business relationships.
Licenses affect scope but do not replace discovery of institutional needs.

sampleQuestions.question: Which statement best describes the intended scope of Education Cloud solutions?
options: Support the learner relationship over time
Scheduling every classroom and faculty member
Delivering all course content and online assessments
Managing academic staff payroll and contracts
sampleQuestions.explanation: Education-focused Salesforce solutions can support relationships and processes across the learner lifecycle.
whyWrong: Classroom scheduling may require another system or specialized tool.
Course content and assessments are commonly handled by an LMS.
Payroll and staff contracts are human resources functions.

sampleQuestions.question: A client wants to know whether a managed package like Admissions Connect is compatible with their existing Education Cloud setup before installing it. What should the consultant review first?
options: The documented compatibility notes for the current configuration
Install it right away immediately without checking anything first at all
Only the sticker price of the managed package
Whether the package's name sounds relevant to the project
sampleQuestions.explanation: Reviewing documented compatibility and configuration considerations before installing a managed package is part of understanding Education Cloud's configuration capabilities and constraints.
whyWrong: Installing first and discovering problems afterward risks breaking a production org.
Price alone says nothing about whether the package fits the existing configuration.
A package's name doesn't establish technical compatibility.

sampleQuestions.question: An institution is rolling out a new Education Cloud implementation and wants end users to actually adopt it instead of reverting to spreadsheets. What should the consultant plan for, beyond the technical build?
options: Assume a technically correct build guarantees adoption on its own, with nothing else needed
Change management, training, and adoption planning as part of the rollout
Skip user testing entirely to save time before launch
Avoid documentation since requirements rarely change anyway
sampleQuestions.explanation: A successful implementation plans for governance, change management, and adoption, not just the technical configuration, this is explicitly part of Implementation Strategies and Best Practices.
whyWrong: A technically sound build can still fail if users don't adopt it, adoption needs deliberate planning.
Skipping testing increases the risk of deploying a broken or unusable solution.
Documentation supports long-term maintainability even when requirements seem stable.

sampleQuestions.question: A university needs to migrate a large volume of historical student records into Education Cloud as part of an implementation. What should the consultant evaluate first?
options: Whether the records can be renamed in bulk
Only the color scheme of the destination object's page layout
Data volume, quality, and migration considerations for the target data model
Whether the old system had a mobile app
sampleQuestions.explanation: Evaluating data volume, data quality, and how records will map and migrate into the Education Cloud data model is a core data management consideration for an implementation.
whyWrong: Bulk renaming isn't the key migration concern, data volume and mapping quality are.
Page layout color has nothing to do with a data migration's success.
Whether the old system had a mobile app is irrelevant to migrating its data.

sampleQuestions.question: Leadership wants a report showing enrollment trends over time, broken out by program and recruitment source. What should the consultant consider when choosing a reporting approach?
options: Always recommend the single most expensive analytics product available
Assume reporting is never needed in an education implementation
Assume only the Salesforce mobile app can ever produce a report
Whether standard reports and dashboards meet the need, or more is justified
sampleQuestions.explanation: Distinguishing between what standard reporting can deliver and when a more advanced analytics solution is actually justified is the core skill tested in the Analytics domain.
whyWrong: Recommending the most expensive option regardless of fit ignores the actual requirement.
Reporting on trends like this is exactly the kind of need education implementations address.
Reports and dashboards aren't limited to the mobile app.

sampleQuestions.question: An institution's student information system (SIS) needs to stay in sync with Education Cloud so that enrollment changes in one system appear in the other. What should the consultant evaluate first?
options: Whether the SIS login page looks visually appealing
Whether both systems happen to use the same font
Assume systems always sync automatically with zero configuration
The integration pattern needed to connect the two systems reliably
sampleQuestions.explanation: Evaluating integration considerations, such as sync direction, frequency, and data mapping, for connecting an external system like an SIS is a core Integration and Data Management skill.
whyWrong: A login page's appearance has nothing to do with whether two systems can integrate reliably.
Matching fonts is irrelevant to system integration.
Systems don't sync automatically without deliberate integration configuration.
